Release notesKTPH000
What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.
Enterprise policyKTPH000

KTPH002Administrators can now manage korTTY through a policy fileKTPH003 — a KTPH000 in the installation directory (admin-writable only) can restrict servers users may connect to (allow/deny lists with host globs, ports, single IPs, CIDR networks and IP ranges, enforced for terminals, SFTP, QuickConnect, jump hosts and scheduled jobs), disable or restrict features (AI Agent/Chat/Swarm/Planning, Teamwork, plugins, update checks, telemetry, terminal recording), force the master password and host-key verification, confine korTTY to an internal clipboard so text copied in other applications cannot be pasted into korTTY (while copy KTPH006 paste within korTTY keeps working), control logging (directory, format as text or JSON lines, retention, gzip compression and rotation caps), and preconfigure read-only AI profiles (with encrypted API keys via KTPH001), local AI models, script headers and teamwork sources. Rules target individual users, policy-defined groups or OS/AD groups with user KTPH007 group KTPH008 everyone precedence; locked settings appear grayed out with a "Managed by your organization" hint, and an invalid policy file puts korTTY into a fail-safe lockdown instead of silently enforcing nothing. See KTPH004Enterprise policyKTPH005.
File browserKTPH000

KTPH000The menu-bar File Browser was rebuilt as a proper file managerKTPH001 — the docked sidebar (KTPH002View → File BrowserKTPH003) gained a navigation toolbar (back / forward / up / home / refresh, new folder / file), an editable path bar that can root the tree at any directory including above your home folder, a filter field, type-aware icons with a symbolic-link badge, and a footer that counts the folders, files and selection in the current directory. See KTPH004File browserKTPH005.

KTPH001Faster and safer to useKTPH002 — directories load in the background so a large or network-mounted folder no longer freezes the window, refreshing keeps expanded folders open, and you can sort by name, size or date. Inline rename (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004), KTPH005Copy PathKTPH006, keyboard navigation, and dragging files into the panel to copy or move them were added.

KTPH000Delete asks first — Trash or permanentKTPH001 — deleting an entry now prompts to either move it to the system Trash (reversible) or delete it permanently, instead of silently removing it forever. Copy, move, archive and delete all run in the background so a large folder no longer freezes the window.
KTPH000The panel remembers itselfKTPH001 — its side, width, KTPH002show hidden filesKTPH003 state and last directory are restored on the next launch.
KTPH000The SFTP file manager matches the new lookKTPH001 — its toolbar and file-type icons now use the same icon set and styling as the file browser (no change to how it works).
Jump server (bastion host)KTPH000

KTPH000Jump server hopping is now implementedKTPH001 — a connection with an enabled jump server is routed through the bastion: korTTY authenticates to the jump host with its own credentials, opens a tunnel, and opens the real SSH session to the target through it. Previously the Jump Server tab collected host, username and password but discarded them on save and connected straight to the target — a connection could look bastion-routed while going direct. The tab now persists every field (password encrypted with the master password) and adds an authentication selector for password or an unencrypted SSH key file.

KTPH000The bastion is verified, and credentials are kept separateKTPH001 — the jump host's key goes through the same trust-on-first-use prompt and pinning as any other host, the target is still verified under its own name through the tunnel, and neither host is ever offered the other's password or key. The write-only KTPH002Auto-CommandKTPH003 field was removed; a real tunnel supersedes the "type ssh on the bastion" pattern it stood for.
KTPH000SFTP now routes through the jump server tooKTPH001 — file transfer connections hop through the bastion the same way terminal sessions do.

KTPH000Mosh with a jump server is refused up frontKTPH001 — a Mosh session runs over UDP, which the bastion's SSH tunnel cannot forward; previously the SSH bootstrap succeeded and the session then stalled with no data. Connecting now fails immediately with a clear message, and the Jump Server tab warns as soon as the combination is configured. SFTP for such connections still routes through the bastion.
SSH host-key verificationKTPH000

KTPH000Opt out of host-key verification, per connection, per group, or globallyKTPH001 — for lab or throwaway hosts, korTTY can accept an unknown host key without the first-use prompt. It is an KTPH002accept-newKTPH003 relaxation, not blind trust: a key that differs from one already pinned for that host is still hard-blocked, so a man-in-the-middle on a host you have connected to before is still caught. The three scopes resolve in precedence order — a per-connection override (Connection Manager editor and Quick Connect: KTPH004Use defaultKTPH005 / KTPH006VerifyKTPH007 / KTPH008Don't verifyKTPH009) wins over a per-group toggle (right-click a group → KTPH010Disable host key verificationKTPH011), which wins over the global KTPH012Settings → Terminal → Disable host key verification for all connectionsKTPH013. Off by default. A jump server's own host key is always verified strictly, regardless of the target's setting.
Master passwordKTPH000

KTPH001Optional passwordless auto-login for test environmentsKTPH002 — a new KTPH003Configuration → Global Settings → Security → Disable master password prompt on startupKTPH004 option makes korTTY remember the master password (stored only obfuscated, with owner-only permissions, in KTPH000) and unlock the vault automatically at startup, so encrypted data such as AI profiles and SSH passwords stays usable with no prompt. On a brand-new profile it even sets up a default password so the app can start with zero input. It is insecure by design — the file permissions are the only protection — and meant for throwaway/test setups such as a VM: korTTY asks you to confirm before enabling it, keeps a warning visible while it is on, and an enterprise policy that forces the master password overrides it. Off by default.
Guide translationKTPH000

KTPH000The offline guide can now be translated by a local AI profileKTPH001 — KTPH002Configuration → Global Settings → Translation → Guide translationKTPH003 translates the bundled offline guide (the same site this documentation is part of), including its in-page search, into the target language chosen above, using an AI profile rather than the translation-provider API. Translation runs in the background: it keeps going after Settings is closed, shows a progress bar, percentage and time-remaining estimate at the right end of the menu bar, can be cancelled and resumed without losing progress, and korTTY asks before quitting while it is running. After an update that changed the guide, korTTY offers once to bring an existing translation up to date, re-translating only what actually changed. See KTPH004TranslationKTPH005.

KTPH000Estimate duration before committing to a full translationKTPH001 — a new KTPH002Estimate durationKTPH003 button measures the chosen AI profile against a real sample of the guide and projects how long translating everything remaining would take, without waiting out the full run.

KTPH000A warning appears before translating with a reasoning modelKTPH001 — such models spend most of their output "thinking" rather than translating, which can turn a translation that takes about an hour into one that takes six or more; korTTY detects this from the model's name and warns before starting or estimating, while still allowing you to proceed.
Interface translationKTPH000

KTPH000Any AI profile can now translate the interface stringsKTPH001 — the KTPH002Local AI text profileKTPH003 provider gained its own KTPH004AI profileKTPH005 dropdown, matching the one the guide translation already had. A profile picked there is used whatever its connection mode, so a cloud model (Anthropic, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) or a local CLI profile can generate a language pack, not only an embedded llama.cpp/MLX model. Leaving it on KTPH006Default (local text profile)KTPH007 keeps the previous behaviour: the Text-role profile, and only when it runs a local model — the provider exists for people who do not want their interface strings leaving the machine. When that role holds a cloud or CLI profile, korTTY now names the profile and points at the dropdown instead of reporting a bare "failed to generate language file". See KTPH008TranslationKTPH009.

KTPH000A malformed batch no longer throws away the whole language packKTPH001 — previously one bad reply from the model aborted language-file generation completely and nothing was written at all, even though most strings had translated. The batch is now retried and split in half, and only a string the model never returns in usable form keeps its English text.
ASCII artKTPH000

KTPH000AI-drawn ASCII picturesKTPH001 — the ASCII art tool (KTPH002Tools KTPH008 ASCII Art...KTPH003) gained an KTPH004AI PictureKTPH005 tab: type a subject such as "house" and a model draws it as an ASCII picture, constrained to printable ASCII within 60 columns and 30 lines so it stays readable. KTPH006New variationKTPH007 redraws the same subject with a different treatment — viewing angle, level of detail, line style, scene context or proportions — asking for something different again on each retry, and a transient profile picker lets a single run use a different AI profile without changing your default.

KTPH007Zoomable previewKTPH008 — both tabs share one zoom level, adjustable with the KTPH009+KTPH010 / KTPH011−KTPH012 / KTPH013⟲KTPH014 buttons, KTPH015KTPH000KTPH016+KTPH017KTPH001KTPH018 / KTPH019KTPH002KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH003KTPH022 / KTPH023KTPH004KTPH024+KTPH025KTPH005KTPH026, or KTPH027KTPH006KTPH028 and the scroll wheel over the preview. The level ranges from 50 % to 333 % and is remembered between sessions along with the window position and size.

KTPH000Two tabs instead of one formKTPH001 — the FIGlet banner generator moved into its own KTPH002Text BannerKTPH003 tab, so a banner and a picture keep their own result while you switch, and KTPH004Copy to ClipboardKTPH005 copies whichever tab is open.

KTPH001Fixed: the Lean font was missing from packaged buildsKTPH002 — the style was declared in lowercase while the bundled file is KTPH000, so JAR resource lookup dropped it from the style list on case-sensitive filesystems.
DashboardKTPH000

KTPH005Redesigned dashboard panelKTPH006 — the side panel (KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH003KTPH012) got a full visual and interaction overhaul: a clear panel boundary with its own background, a header with the panel title plus collapse/expand-all and refresh icon buttons, node-type icons for main window, environment, group and connection rows, and bold section rows with dimmed active/total counts. Rows respond to hover and selection (accent stripe), tooltips show KTPH000 and the connection state, and KTPH013KTPH004KTPH014 or double-click focuses the session.

KTPH003Three-state status dots and protocol badgesKTPH004 — each connection row shows a filled green dot while connected, a filled red dot when the connection dropped unexpectedly (including Mosh network interruptions), and a hollow outline after a session ended normally; the old text-glyph status is gone. A small KTPH000 / KTPH001 / KTPH002 badge identifies the transport.

KTPH000Environment groupingKTPH001 — ungrouped connections cluster under the environment of their stored credential (Production, Development, Test, Staging or custom), so multi-stage work stays visually separated.

KTPH000Content-sized, animated panelKTPH001 — the dashboard sizes its width to the longest entry (bounded), animates open and closed instead of popping in, shows a placeholder when no session is open, and reports "connected of total" in a footer. Its colors follow the active App Design, including per-design status-dot palettes.

KTPH000Context menu and group fixesKTPH001 — the connection context menu adds KTPH002FocusKTPH003 and icons for every action. Tabs opened via "open whole group" now correctly appear under their group, and changing a connection's group in the Connection Manager updates open tabs immediately.
Tool windows as tabsKTPH000

KTPH000Management tools can open as tabs in the main windowKTPH001 — a new KTPH002Open tool windows as tabsKTPH003 option in KTPH004Window settingsKTPH005 makes Snippets, the JobScheduler, the AI Manager, Saved Chats, Credential/GPG/SSH key management, the Video Manager, Teamwork settings and the Terminal Effects manager open as tabs beside your terminal sessions instead of separate windows. The tab always opens in the main window whose menu you used, so with several windows open each collects its own tools — for example the AI Manager as a tab in one window and the JobScheduler in another. Reopening a tool focuses its existing tab, while the snippet editor and the AI code analysis open a new tab per snippet/run so several can sit side by side; tool tabs can be reordered and dragged between windows like any other tab. Off by default — nothing changes unless you enable it.
Power managementKTPH000

KTPH001Activity-based power managementKTPH002 — macOS App Nap is suppressed while a Scheduler job, AI request, or terminal input/output is active (with a 60-second terminal-activity tail). Background windows park periodic status updates and design animations, and the Scheduler owns no polling timer when no enabled future run exists. On macOS, system-sleep prevention is delegated to a separate KTPH000 helper so the korTTY process remains eligible for App Nap. On macOS and Windows, KTPH003Configuration KTPH005 Prevent System SleepKTPH004 keeps the computer awake only while a terminal is connected, a future or running Scheduler job exists, or an AI request is active; with none of these activities, system sleep remains available even while the persistent setting is checked. Display sleep is unaffected, and Linux shows the option as not yet supported.
Snippet editorKTPH000

KTPH000Code language and Text language are now two labelled fieldsKTPH001 — the snippet editor's KTPH002LanguageKTPH003 field was renamed to KTPH004Code languageKTPH005, and the AI text-language picker moved up from below the toolbar to sit directly beneath it as KTPH006Text languageKTPH007. Both describe the snippet itself: one the programming language and syntax highlighting, the other the natural language korTTY writes into the code (comments, user-facing strings, spelling).

KTPH001TypeScript is selectableKTPH002 — TypeScript joins the code-language list, with its own KTPH000 extension, Monaco highlighting and Prettier formatting (the formatter already supported it, but no snippet could be marked as TypeScript).

KTPH000Add your own code languagesKTPH001 — a KTPH002+KTPH003 button beside the code-language list takes any language name that is missing and stores it permanently, so it is offered in every future snippet editor. Self-added languages drive the AI prompts and the file extension; highlighting falls back to plain text when korTTY ships no grammar for them.

KTPH004AI suggestion fills both language fieldsKTPH005 — besides the file name and description, KTPH006AI suggestionKTPH007 now also detects the natural language of the snippet's comments and printed output (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, …) and preselects it as the text language, adding it to the list when korTTY has no interface translation for it. A detected code language missing from the list is likewise added instead of being silently dropped.

KTPH000New AI action: Optimize code commentsKTPH001 — available from the KTPH002AI CodeKTPH003 menu and from the editor's right-click menu on a selection. The AI inserts explanations of what the selected code does and why, directly above or beside the lines they belong to and in the language's own comment syntax, replaces outdated or misleading comments, and leaves every executable line untouched. Comments are written in the editor's KTPH004Text languageKTPH005, and the result is shown in the usual before/after preview before it replaces the selection.

KTPH000Automatic analysis diagrams can be switched offKTPH001 — the Full Code Analysis window's diagram pane gained a KTPH002Generate automaticallyKTPH003 checkbox.
